Assumptions: Dry production less lease and plant fuel, divided by marketed production, from the U.S. totals of the model year (0.880 in 2019). Source: Evolved Energy Research, 2024 U.S. Annual Decarbonization Perspective, RIO data input catalog
Assumptions: 10,725 USD per MW of marketed production capacity per year: 10.3 2022 USD/kW-year (``supply_tech_fixed_om``, the same in every scenario) times 1.0413 (CPI-U 2023/2022). Unless ``infra_contraction`` is true, production is not extendable and its fixed O&M only adds to the system cost.

1.01% of the flow is burned as compressor fuel (all compressors gas-fired) and 0.54% leaks per 1000 km. Pipeline length is the great circle distance between the centers of the two states times ``pipeline_length_factor``. Trade pipelines are lossless.

Source: `PyPSA technology-data <https://github.com/PyPSA/technology-data>`_ v0.15.0; `EHB June 2021 <https://natrangroupe.com/sites/default/files/2021-06/European-Hydrogen-Backbone-report-June2021.pdf>`_ Table 35; `EHB November 2023 <https://ehb.eu/files/downloads/EHB-2023-20-Nov-FINAL-design.pdf>`_ Table 1; `Transition Accelerator <https://transitionaccelerator.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/The-Techno-Economics-of-Hydrogen-Pipelines-v2.pdf>`_ Tables 4.1 and 5.1
Assumptions: 8.93 USD per MW and km per year (2023 USD): 1.5%/year fixed O&M (technology-data CH4 pipeline) of the investment of a new 36-inch onshore pipeline. As an H2 pipeline it costs (3.20 MEUR/km + 93 MWe/1000 km * 4.0 MEUR/MWe) / 4.7 GW = 760.0 EUR/MW_LHV/km, with 2023 costs (EHB 2023) and the throughput and compression at 100% capacity (EHB 2021). For natural gas it is scaled by 0.884 / 1.1 to 610.8 EUR/MW_LHV/km: the same pipe carries 1/0.884 times as much energy as methane as it does as H2 (LHV), and an H2 pipeline costs 1.1 times a natural gas pipeline. Divided by the methane HHV/LHV of 1.11 to 550.2 EUR/MW_HHV/km and converted at 1.0817 USD/EUR (2023). Unless ``infra_contraction`` is true, existing pipelines are not extendable and their fixed O&M only adds to the system cost. Trade pipelines carry no fixed O&M.

1,278 USD per MW of injection capacity per year, carried by the charge link: 4%/year of 29.95 2025 EUR/kW, the PyPSA-Eur H2 storage compressor cost divided by 3.12 (volumetric energy density of methane over hydrogen), converted at 1.1306 USD/EUR (2025 average) and divided by 1.06 (CPI-U 2025/2023). The store and well carry no fixed O&M.

1.03% of injected gas is lost, mostly as compressor fuel, the median of the storage injection fuel retention of NGPL (0.84%), National Fuel Gas Supply (0.89%) and Southwest Gas Storage (1.17% and 2.61%). Some retention rates also cover lost and unaccounted-for gas.

Source: `EIA-191 Monthly Underground Natural Gas Storage Report <https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/ngqs/>`_ via `PUDL <https://docs.catalyst.coop/pudl/en/latest/data_sources/eia191.html>`_
Assumptions: Active reservoirs in the latest month of the report, summed per state (or per state and formation). Energy capacity is the total field capacity; the minimum level is total field capacity minus working gas capacity, so the usable range is the working gas capacity. Discharge capacity is the maximum daily delivery; charge capacity is 0.3676 times the discharge capacity (ratio of historical maximum charge and discharge rates). Starts with base gas plus two thirds of the working range. Not extendable unless ``infra_contraction`` is true, which lets the store, injection and withdrawal capacities shrink to zero.
